thesis: Genmab announced today (GlobeNewswire / Genmab IR, Oct 23) that the Phase 3 RAINFOL-02 trial of rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S) in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer met its primary endpoint, with a progression-free-survival hazard ratio of 0.29 in the 584-patient intent-to-treat population (a 71% risk reduction), and its key secondary overall-survival endpoint (HR 0.43), with no new safety signals; the stock rose about 9.5% on 3x volume to a new 52-week high. The counter-case is structural and still open: Genmab faces royalty erosion as its DARZALEX-linked income matures, and Rina-S is not yet approved, with regulatory discussions and the full data presentation still pending, so how much of that gap this asset fills remains to be shown, which keeps this at medium. The DARZALEX royalty arbitrations with Janssen concluded in 2024, and this run found no restatement or other scheduled legal event.
invalidation: Full RAINFOL-02 data or regulators raise a safety or efficacy concern, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$40.00).

thesis: Instacart rose about 9.3% today on 4.8x volume to an all-time high after The Information reported that the company is exploring a sale, has hired a bank and has held preliminary talks with Uber and DoorDash; no transaction or terms have been confirmed by the company, so the move rests on an unconfirmed report. Revenue growth has slowed to about 11%, and with the price already near the consensus target the setup depends on a deal that may not materialize. Instacart settled the FTC delivery-fee case for $60M (stipulated order filed January 2026), and a reported FTC civil investigative demand over AI-driven pricing has no scheduled step found.
invalidation: A confirmed definitive sale agreement at a disclosed premium to the current price.

thesis: Tango fell about 16% today on 4.1x volume despite presenting updated Phase 1/2 data for vopimetostat with daraxonrasib in pancreatic cancer (82% objective response rate and 88% 9-month progression-free survival in 22 patients); the update largely confirmed results first reported in June, and the response rate was lower than the 92% reported then, after a run-up from about $21.89 to $27.93 ahead of the data. The front-line Phase 3 is not expected to start until 1H 2027 and Q3 results are due around Nov 4. With the data viewed as incremental and slightly weaker, the evidence is unresolved. The June 2026 $690M equity offering falls outside the 90-day dilution window, and the 10-Q reports no material litigation.
invalidation: Larger-cohort data that holds the June response rate, or a confirmed Phase 3 start.

thesis: Robert Half reported Q3 2026 on Oct 22 (8-K): revenue of about $1.36B was flat on an adjusted basis, EPS rose to $0.49 from $0.43 and beat the $0.47 consensus, and Talent Solutions returned to adjusted growth (+2%) for the first time since 2022, which suggests the staffing cycle may be turning; the stock rose about 21.8% today on 3.8x volume to a new 52-week high. The counter-case is that total revenue is still flat and one quarter of low-single-digit growth in a cyclical hiring market is not yet a trend, so this stays medium. Litigation found is older wage-and-hour and background-check matters (an FCRA settlement received final approval in May 2025), with no scheduled 2026 events, and no restatement was found.
invalidation: Q4 results show Talent Solutions growth reversing, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$37.68).

thesis: RingCentral reported Q3 2026 on Oct 22 (8-K): total revenue rose 5.9% to $676M, above its $664-670M guidance, subscriptions revenue rose 6.0% to $653M, the non-GAAP operating margin expanded about 190bp to 24.7%, and management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $2.650-2.657B in revenue (from $2.635-2.646B), $5.07-5.12 in non-GAAP EPS (from $4.96-5.10) and $620-630M in free cash flow, while ARR from customers using a paid native AI product doubled to nearly 15% of the total and gross debt fell to about $1B. The stock gained about 5% today on 3x volume after trading as high as $98 in a broad tech selloff. The strongest counter-case is competitive: growth is only about 6% in a crowded cloud-communications market, but the read does not depend on fast growth, since the beat, the margin expansion and the raised EPS and free-cash-flow guidance all come from the company's own disclosed results at that growth rate. A January 2026 law-firm investigation notice has no filed claim, the 10-Qs show no material proceeding, and this run found no restatement.
invalidation: Q4 revenue or margin falls short of the raised guidance, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$79.42).

thesis: Crown Castle rose about 9.1% today on 3.6x volume on reports of SpaceX's terrestrial-network ambitions, a sector-wide tower-stock move rather than a company disclosure; SpaceX has described building around existing towers rather than on them, and this run could not confirm the reported cell-site talks. The company's own Q3 2026 results (Oct 21) were mixed: site rental revenue fell 5% and net income 12% and revenue and EPS were slightly below consensus, while AFFO rose 8% and the full-year outlook was raised. The 2020 restatement and related litigation fall outside the 3-year governance window.
invalidation: A confirmed SpaceX leasing agreement with Crown Castle, or site rental revenue returning to growth.

thesis: Rexford reported Q3 2026 on Oct 22 (8-K): Core FFO of $0.60 per share was flat year over year, management raised 2026 Core FFO guidance, completed $1.5B of dispositions year to date, repaid $485M of debt and cut net debt to adjusted EBITDA to 3.8x from 4.5x, and the CEO cited improving infill Southern California industrial fundamentals; the stock rose about 6.7% today on 2.6x volume. The counter-case is that per-share earnings are not yet growing (net income fell to $0.07 from $0.37 a year ago and Core FFO was flat) and the dispositions shrink the earnings base, so the recovery is still pending and this stays medium. The FY2025 10-K reports no material legal proceedings, and this run found no restatement or leadership change.
invalidation: Q4 results or 2027 guidance show Core FFO declining, or a close back below the 200-day average.

thesis: Glacier Bancorp reported Q3 2026 on Oct 22 (8-K): record net income of $105M (+54% year over year), diluted EPS of $0.80, and net interest income up 29% year over year to $290M, with loans of $21.6B and deposits of $25.3B; the stock rose about 3.9% today on 2.3x volume. But the $0.80 EPS appears to fall short of at least one pre-report estimate ($0.86), and the year-over-year growth partly reflects a larger balance sheet, so the evidence is mixed rather than a clear beat. The company's filings describe only ordinary-course litigation, and this run found no restatement.
invalidation: Q4 results show margin compression or credit deterioration, or a close back below the 200-day average.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 19). This run found no new company disclosure: the stock edged up to $17.29 near its 52-week high, commentary points to renewed organic momentum in the VWR distribution business and improving bioprocessing orders, and UBS assumed coverage at Neutral with a $16 target. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: the motion to dismiss the securities class action is still being briefed with no ruling date, and Q3 results on Oct 28 are a pending binary event, so this stays medium.
invalidation: Q3 results on Oct 28 miss or guidance is cut, an adverse class-action ruling, or a close back below the 20-day average (~$15.77).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF rebounded about 6.4% today to $13.89, attributed to continued positive reaction to the Q3 report (adjusted EBITDA of $612M vs the company's $575M guidance, Q4 guided to about $715M, 2027 above $4B), Wells Fargo raising its target to $17 (Overweight), and a director's roughly $100K open-market purchase; this run found no new company disclosure. The counter-case named in the prior thesis is still open, since the outlook depends on contract changes and steel-price forecasts, along with the unconfirmed reports of tariff pressure on the Stelco unit, so this stays medium.
invalidation: Steel prices or contract pricing weaken enough to put the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook at risk, a confirmed material Stelco shutdown or forced sale, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.12).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). This run found no new company disclosure; the stock slipped about 2.5% to $36.50, still above its pre-announcement level, and the thesis rests on the Oct 21 CLARITY-1/CLARITY-2 Phase 3 results for brepocitinib in non-infectious uveitis, a drug already approved for dermatomyositis. The counter-case named in the prior thesis is still open: the uveitis sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027, so approval for this indication and its commercial weight remain pending, and Q2 fiscal results on Nov 9 are the next scheduled event, so this stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).
